sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vivek Kumar Birla,J.
Hon'ble Surendra Singh-I,J.
1.

Heard Sri Sanjeev Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the petitioner and Ms. Manju Thakur,
learned A.G.A for the State respondents.

2. The relief sought in this petition is for quashing of the F.I.R. dated 5.4.2023, registered as Case Crime No. 215 of 2023, under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station Hata,
District Kushi Nagar.

entities.text:
Police Station Hata,
District Kushi Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further prayer has been made not to arrest the petitioner in the aforesaid case.

3. Crux of the argument of learned counsel for the petitioner is that the petitioner has sold his Yogendra Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33662597/
1 property purchased by him in the year 2018 and he has not committed any offence.

entities.text: Yogendra Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The dispute is purely civil in nature and the petitioner has not played any fraud.

He further sought to argue that co-accused Byas Maddheshiya has been granted indulgence by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Misc Writ Petition No. 6629 of 2023 on 1.5.2023 and another co-accused Manish has also been granted indulgence by this Court in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 7681 of 2023 and therefore, the petitioner herein is also entitled for the same relief.
4.

entities.text: Criminal Misc Writ Petition No. 6629 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 7681 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Learned AGA opposed the prayer for quashing of the FIR, which discloses cognizable offence.
5. We find that co-accused Byas Maddheshiya has been granted indulgence by this Court on the argument that he has introduced the first informant to certain persons who have executed the sale deed.

We find that the petitioner herein is the person who has actually executed the sale deed and we also find that in both the sale deeds boundaries are same, therefore, the case of the petitioner herein is not on the parity of the co-accused, who have been granted indulgence.
6.
Perusal of the impugned first information report prima facie also reveals commission of cognizable offence by the petitioner herein.

7. Therefore, in view of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana and others vs. Bhajan Lal and others, 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335 and M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt.
Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2021 SC 1918 and in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.3262/2021 (Leelavati Devi @ Leelawati & another vs. the State of Uttar Pradesh) decided on 07.10.2021, no case has been made out for interference with the impugned first information report.
